title: Openwater deployment timetable and causeway notes — Jun 2026 (draft)
content:
Purpose:
- Compact, read-for-shift deployment timetable and annotated notes for the Openwater feature roll (June 2026).
- Designed for a staged canary across regions with a single quiet-window handoff.
- This is a working doc: smoke steps + staffing + minimal release notes draft; keep it lean for on-call handoff.

Scope and constraints:
- Targets: hosted API + dedicated inference pools. No private (on-prem) changes in this rollout.
- Primary risk: KV cache incompatibility between quantized variant and baseline serving.
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 220ms during canary, p95 <= 350ms at 100% traffic.
- Cost guardrail: abort if sustained token cost delta > +18% for 30m without quality improvement signoffs.

Timeline (local times are PST unless noted) — 2026-06-28 (launch day):
- 08:00 - Ops sync (15m): final checklist, confirm readiness, channel #deploy-openwater. Owners: Asha (lead), Marco (telemetry).
- 08:20 - Preflight smoke on staging: basic generation tests x5, KV warmup. Owner: Evelyn.
- 08:40 - Canary 1 (0.5% global): routing to new model variant in us-west-2. 20m steady window. Owner: Jonah.
- 09:00 - Telemetry review checkpoint (15m): p50/p95 latencies, error rate, tail token throughput. Owners: Marco + SRE.
- 09:20 - Canary 2 (2%): expand if metrics stable for 20m. Owner: Asha.
- 09:50 - Canary 3 (10%): expand if stable for 30m. Owner: Asha.
- 10:30 - Regional soak (us-west-2 full, eu-west-1 at 5%): monitor for 60m. Owners: Ops pair.
- 12:00 - Decision: proceed to ramp to 50% or rollback. Use decision matrix below.
- 14:00 - If green, ramp 50% -> 100% by 15:30. Gradual weighted shifts, watch error cohorts.
- 16:00 - Post-rollout validation, tagging, and release notes publish.

Staffing and rotation:
- Launch lead: Asha Patel (08:00-16:30 PST).
- Telemetry & Metrics: Marco Ruiz (08:00-12:00 PST), backup: Priya Menon (12:00-16:30 PST).
- Canary steward: Jonah Kim (hands-on traffic shifts).
- QA smoke: Evelyn Zhao (preflight & post-shift verification).
- Pager coverage: on-call SRE + serving-runtime engineer on 1-hour overlap.

Preflight checklist (must be green before 08:40):
- [ ] Service configs pushed to canary lane (Asha).
- [ ] Model variant validated in internal harness (Evelyn).
- [ ] Canary routing rules tested in staging (Jonah).
- [ ] KV cache pre-warm script run against representative prefixes (Evelyn).
- [ ] Telemetry dashboards (latency, errors, cost) loaded and annotated (Marco).
- [ ] Rollback playbook visible in channel + runbook link shared (Asha).
- [ ] Stakeholders alerted: growth, product PM, customer success (email + slack).

Decision matrix (automated + manual gate):
- Abort immediately if:
  - Error rate spike > 0.5% absolute and sustained for 5m with increasing trend.
  - P95 latency > 400ms sustained for 10m.
  - Quality regression: automated eval score drop > 7 points on critical prompt set (tracked by eval job).
- Pause and investigate if:
  - Cost delta > +12% for 20m but quality neutral.
  - Tail (99th) latency increases by > 60% but p95 within SLO.
- Proceed if:
  - No abort conditions and key KPIs stable for the prescribed steady window per canary step.

Rollback steps (fast path):
- Step 1: Stop traffic to canary variant (Jonah).
- Step 2: Route 100% to last known-good model (Ops).
- Step 3: Trigger incident channel and create a postmortem ticket assigned to feature owner.
- Step 4: Run cold KV purge on canary machines if cache corruption suspected (Evelyn).

Smoke tests (short form, to be executed after each ramp):
- 5 generation queries with short/long context, check token continuity.
- Embeddings sanity on 10 docs (compare vector norms).
- Function/tool call handoff scenario (if used by route).
- Rate-limited burst: short 1s/10qps spike to ensure throttles behave.

Telemetry & dashboards to watch (links in linked_artifacts):
- Latency heatmap by region and model variant.
- Error rate by HTTP path + model id.
- Token cost per minute and 30m rolling average.
- Quality regression evaluator stream: critical prompts pass rate.
- KV cache hit ratio and eviction events.

Release notes (draft — publish at 16:00 if green):
- Title: Openwater: improved prefix-KV handling and quantized variant rollout (June 28, 2026)
- Summary: Gradual rollout of the Openwater serving variant with KV-cache pre-warm and attention-kernel micro-optimizations. Most customers will see similar latency with reduced variance; unit cost expected to drop ~6% at steady state for high prefix reuse workloads.
- User impact: No API changes. Short, transient increases in latency may occur during rolling traffic shifts; requests will be retried automatically by client libraries.
- Admin/ops notes: Feature gated by model id openwater-v1. Pin older model with modelId=retained-2026-05 if rollback needed.
- Known issues: Edge-case prompt truncation observed in synthetic evals for sequences > 12k tokens under quantized paths (low frequency). Workaround: use modelId=retained-2026-05 for long-form workflows until patch.

Postmortem & follow-ups (Asha to assign within 48h if any abort):
- Capture timeline and metrics snapshot for each phase.
- If aborted: short retro call within 24h to capture lessons and reconvene a remediation plan.
- Action items list (sample):
  - Investigate KV eviction pattern on quantized nodes (Evelyn) — due 2026-07-05.
  - Add canary automation for 5-min micro-checks (Marco) — due 2026-07-12.
  - Measure client retry patterns and UX note (GTM) (Priya) — due 2026-07-09.

Open questions / TODOs (pre-launch):
- Do we need an additional twilight window for APAC region to reduce timezone risk? (ask product)
- Confirm whether Dedicated customers on legacy routing require a separate rollout lane. (ops + account execs)
- Who owns the final release note copy for blog post? (PM suggestion: Lina Ortiz)

Slack templates (copy-paste for launch channel):
- Preflight 08:00: "Launching Openwater preflight in 20m — owners: Asha, Marco, Evelyn, Jonah. Channel = #deploy-openwater. If you are not on the staffing roster, please stand by for notifications only."
- Canary step alert: "Canary 1 -> 0.5% routing completed. Telemetry green? reply with ✅ or 🛑. Owner: Jonah."
- Abort alert: "ABORT: Openwater canary. Rolling back to retained-2026-05. See incident RED-XXXX."

Appendix: quick commands and links
- Canary routing (example): curl -XPOST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/traffic-shift -d '{"model":"openwater-v1","weight":0.005, "region":"us-west-2"}'  # ops use only
- Eval harness job: ci.redwood/internal/evals/openwater/nightly
- PM contact: Lina Ortiz (lina@redwood.ai)

Notes to self: keep runbook stripped to essentials, avoid long prose. If launch slips, re-run preflight and re-check KV warmups.

End of doc.
